why: This file held 15 vectors and 37 steps. Nothing read it and nothing regenerated it — check-drift-parity.ts has always read the copy in the Worker directory. It was a fossil: correct on the day it was written, with no mechanism to stay that way, and no way to tell the difference by looking at it.

Both sets were compared before it was retired. It carried no verdict the generated set lacked. It did carry five verdict SEQUENCES the generated set had lost, all two or three steps long — including the two-strike self-report escalation, and an ungrammatical arriving on the step straight after ground. Every case in the generator had been six steps or longer, which made the START of a run the least covered part of the instrument. The start is the part every real run executes.
Those five cases now live in gen-drift-vectors.py under 'SHORT runs'. The generated set went from 9 vectors to 14, and 52 steps to 64.
why_a_pointer_and_not_a_deletion: The keys 'vectors' and 'sdk_version' are deliberately absent. Anything still reading this file raises a KeyError naming the key it wanted, rather than quietly consuming 15 stale vectors and reporting agreement. A file that is wrong should be harder to use than one that is right. Deleting it would achieve that too — this way the record of what happened travels with the artifact, which is the argument for laserstore existing at all.
